headline: Large User Grid Cost Shift
short_summary: This bill directs the State Corporation Commission to establish rates that shift the costs of increasing electric generating capacity to large energy users, primarily data centers, rather than residential customers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, environmental groups, U.S. Sen. Mark Warner.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: Virginia Governor Signs Dominion-Backed Bills to Shift Data Center Costs
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed legislation directing regulators to assign electricity costs to data centers, ensuring residential customers do not unfairly bear these generation and distribution expenses. This aims to address rising utility bills caused by data centers' high energy demands and grid infrastructure needs.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates water suppliers to report the volume of potable and reclaimed water provided to data centers, enhancing transparency on the industry's water consumption.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservationists, Senator Kannan Srinivasan, Delegate Elizabeth Guzman, Delegate Shelly Simonds, Potomac Conservancy.
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Approve Legislation to Track Water Use by Data Centers
news_summary: The Virginia General Assembly passed SB 553, requiring water suppliers to report water usage by data centers to the State Water Control Board. This legislation aims to provide crucial data for understanding the industry's impact on Virginia's water resources, as data centers can consume millions of gallons daily.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for new high-energy use facilities, including sound profiles and potential impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites, giving localities more control over data center siting.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental and conservation groups, historic preservation advocates, farmland protection groups, Virginia League of Conservation Voters.
opponents: Data center developers and tech industry trade groups, chambers of commerce, commercial real estate associations, pro-growth business or utility groups.
news_headline: Virginia Bill Requires Data Center Site Assessments for Noise and Other Impacts
news_summary: HB 153 requires local governments to review potential impacts, including noise and effects on nearby homes and schools, before approving new data centers using 100 megawatts or more. This legislation empowers localities to make informed decisions that align with community plans and zoning rules.
